rules.notes: Every in-scope URL must be collected or explicitly reported as blocked.
EN/PT route pairs and language attributes must be consistent.
PT-BR is canonical. EN must preserve PT page family, section order, components, CTAs, product truth, footer/legal blocks, and SEO role; translation alone does not establish parity.
EN must be grammatically reviewed, free of accidental PT content/URLs, and aligned to the PT canonical page purpose; content similarity alone is insufficient.
PT and EN require observed browser computed-style and geometry parity. A screenshot may support context but cannot replace DOM/CSS evidence.
Cards, grids, containers, header, footer, sidebar state, and page-family components must be inventoried and compared explicitly.
Required viewport states must be observed on both canonical PT and target EN pages; unavailable states fail closed.
Logo/name identity must match the approved observed standard.
Do not infer font family, size, weight, or line height.
Computed colors and contrast require browser evidence.
Container, spacing, overflow, and alignment require computed geometry.
Canonical, hreflang, title, description, and indexability must be observed.
Headings, labels, alt text, landmarks, contrast, and focus are audited from evidence; heading levels are evaluated against the page-family template, not globally normalized.
Internal, legal, language, and external links must be checked read-only.
Product status claims are profile-configured and never inferred from user text.
